05

Solution Design

Build a structured ServiceNow Catalog Item with dynamic fields, validation, approval routing, and automated fulfillment.

06

Detailed Workflow / Architecture

Submission creates the RITM before approval. The approval controls whether fulfillment work proceeds; it does not create the RITM after the decision.

REQ → RITM → SCTASK

  1. REQsc_request

    The parent order. One REQ can contain multiple requested items; one item finishing does not mean every item in the order is complete.

  2. RITMsc_req_item

    The requested item. Its request reference links to the REQ; variables, approvals, and the fulfillment flow belong to the item.

  3. SCTASKsc_task

    An actionable fulfillment task. Its request_item reference links to the RITM. An item may need zero, one, or multiple tasks.

08

Implementation Approach

  1. 01

    Build a reusable request model

    Use a shared requester/contact variable set and item-specific service options. Define variable names consistently so scripts and flows can consume the same contract across related items.

  2. 02

    Guide the form

    Use UI Policies for show/hide and mandatory behavior, including reverse conditions when a choice changes. Reserve Catalog Client Scripts for interactions that need logic beyond those policies.

  3. 03

    Validate and orchestrate

    Check required values and permitted combinations on the server as well as the form. Start the item flow on the RITM, resolve approvals, and create catalog tasks linked through request_item after approval.

  4. 04

    Reuse fulfillment patterns

    Parameterize a subflow with the RITM and configured group for repeatable task creation. Wait for the correct task outcome, update the item, and notify relevant participants once per meaningful transition.

09

Technical Logic

Dynamic variables

A selected service determines which dependent variables are visible and required. Clear or ignore stale hidden answers according to the service contract, and validate the final combination again when processing.

Reusable behavior

Keep common requester fields in variable sets, common task orchestration in subflows, and item-specific decisions in configuration. Avoid duplicating the same script across every item.

Fulfillment and closure

Create one or more SCTASK records only for approved work. Check required tasks, preserve unsuccessful outcomes, and let the parent request lifecycle account for all requested items.

10

Technical Challenges & Decisions

UI Policy versus Client Script

Prefer declarative policies for field visibility and mandatory rules. Do not implement the same rule in both places, which makes conflicts and maintenance harder.

Shared changes have shared impact

A variable-set or subflow change can affect multiple items. Test the consumers before moving the configuration to another instance.

No successful closure on rejection

Rejected or cancelled requests stop the approved fulfillment branch. Failed tasks need an explicit recovery or incomplete path instead of automatic successful closure.

11

Testing Approach

Proposed validation scenarios and expected results for an isolated ServiceNow test environment.

Change service options repeatedly
Correct fields appear, mandatory rules reverse, and hidden stale values are handled consistently.
Bypass client-side validation
Server-side processing rejects invalid or incompatible values.
Approve, reject, or cancel
Only approved requests produce the intended catalog tasks.
Shared variable set reused
All consuming items retain their expected form and flow behavior.
Task completion and failure
RITM and REQ outcomes remain consistent, with no duplicate notifications.
12

A standardized request experience with automated workflow and reduced repetitive administrative steps.
